def is_covered_by_n_lines(points, n):
    if not points:
        return True
    if n == 0:
        return not points
    
    # Try all possible lines formed by pairs of points
    # Also include lines formed by a single point (vertical/horizontal)
    lines = []
    pts = list(points)
    for i in range(len(pts)):
        for j in range(i + 1, len(pts)):
            p1, p2 = pts[i], pts[j]
            # Line defined by p1, p2: (y2-y1)x - (x2-x1)y + x2y1 - y2x1 = 0
            a = p2[1] - p1[1]
            b = p1[0] - p2[0]
            c = p2[0]*p1[1] - p2[1]*p1[0]
            lines.append((a, b, c))
    
    # For cases where a line might contain only one point
    for p in pts:
        lines.append((1, 0, -p[0]))
        lines.append((0, 1, -p[1]))

    # Use backtracking to see if n lines can cover all points
    def can_cover(remaining_pts, lines_left):
        if not remaining_pts:
            return True
        if lines_left == 0:
            return False
        
        # Pick a point and try all lines that cover it
        p = remaining_pts[0]
        for line in lines:
            a, b, c = line
            if a*p[0] + b*p[1] + c == 0:
                new_remaining = [pt for pt in remaining_pts if not (a*pt[0] + b*pt[1] + c == 0)]
                if can_cover(new_remaining, lines_left - 1):
                    return True
        return False

    return can_cover(pts, n)
